section: report_public.md line 466 to end (The Invisible Part, Banff, Appendices A-N with E absent, References & Methodology)

claims.claim: The two data problems 'can both be fixed'
About half of all Alberta votes are now cast before election day (advance, mobile, special ballots)
claims.found: 47.5% of 2023 votes are Advance/Mobile/Special
claims.note: 'about half' is fair rounding of 47.5%

claims.claim: Elections Alberta reports advance/mobile/special results as totals per electoral division, not per Voting Area
claims.found: EA released Advance, Mobile, Special-Ballot results only at ED level

claims.claim: Roughly 810,000 NDP and UCP votes cast in 2023 cannot be pinned to any neighbourhood
claims.note: derived figure; matches the 47.5% advance share. analysis/review/swarm_audit_2026-10-29.md row 147 flagged the old 395,000 figure; this text is the corrected one

claims.claim: EA checks every advance voter against a voters list tying each voter to a Voting Area, so the information exists at the moment of voting
claims.found: ELS entry carries each voter's home VA; the link is not carried into the count
claims.note: report hedges as 'our understanding'; the finding file says whether EA internally retains VA-level advance totals is unconfirmed (EA, R. Mok, 2026-05-19, pointed only to the Statement of Vote)

claims.claim: 'no change to the voting process would be required, only a change to what EA reports'
claims.note: conditional policy inference (Election Act s.112(2) exception discussed in the VA043 finding)

claims.claim: A Voting Area in northern Lesser Slave Lake covers 4,832 km2
claims.found: Geographic area: 4,832 km2

claims.claim: 4,832 km2 is 'more than four-fifths the size of Prince Edward Island'
claims.source: web: PEI area ~5,656-5,686 km2, as cited in analysis/review/swarm_audit_2026-10-29.md row 501
claims.note: verified_by: web (via the swarm-audit citation of Wikipedia / PEI Annual Statistical Review; not re-fetched). The earlier 'larger than PEI' wording was corrected

claims.claim: Not one vote in 2023 was cast at an election-day poll in that VA
claims.found: Election-day votes: NDP 0, UCP 0; only VA in ED 70 with no election-day activity

claims.claim: All votes there came by mobile poll or special ballot
claims.found: 'Voting mechanism: mobile poll only'
claims.note: source says mobile poll only; adding 'or special ballot' is not separately sourced but is harmless

claims.claim: 844 residents of that VA
claims.found: 844 persons, 2021 Census
claims.note: 844 is total population (includes non-voters); the sentence says 'residents', so it stands

claims.claim: The commission first considered eliminating Lesser Slave Lake and merging it into a larger riding (interim report)
claims.found: 'the restoration of the Lesser Slave Lake electoral division, which the interim Report had eliminated'

claims.claim: The minority report counts at least 56 public submissions on keeping Lesser Slave Lake
claims.found: 'At least 56 submissions emphasized that the region constitutes a coherent community of interest'

claims.claim: Many of those submissions came from Indigenous communities in the northern part of the riding
claims.found: The passage cites one submission mentioning 'a significant Indigenous population' but does not say many of the 56 came from Indigenous communities
claims.note: searched final report, findings/ and analysis/methodology; no count of submitter origin found

claims.claim: The division was kept by invoking s.15(2) of the Electoral Boundaries Commission Act
claims.found: Lesser Slave Lake -45.4%, 4 of 5 criteria, Pass on both maps

claims.claim: s.15(2): up to four ridings meeting at least three of five criteria may be as much as 50% below the average population
claims.found: 'no more than 4 ... at least 3 of the following criteria ... as much as 50% below the average population'

claims.claim: The five criteria: large area, distance from Edmonton, no town over 8,000, an Indian reserve or Metis settlement, a stretch of provincial border
claims.found: (a) area >20,000 km2 or surveyed >15,000; (b) >150 km from Legislature; (c) no town >8000; (d) reserve or Metis settlement; (e) boundary coterminous with provincial boundary

claims.claim: 'The published vote data still cannot show how those communities voted'
claims.found: votes enter the ED advance/mobile total with no VA attribution

claims.claim: The commission's interim report folded Lesser Slave Lake into a larger riding; both final maps restored it and protected it under s.15(2)
claims.found: Lesser Slave Lake invoked s.15(2) on Majority (-45.4%) and Minority (-45.4%)

claims.claim: The minority used another protected slot on Rocky Mountain House-Banff Park, drawing its boundary through Banff National Park
claims.found: minority's third s.15(2) slot = Rocky Mountain House-Banff Park (-30.3%)

claims.claim: The majority described the park stretch as a place 'where no one lives'
claims.found: 'taking part of Banff National Park, where no one lives' / 'A large portion of Banff National Park where no one lives'
claims.note: quote matches word for word

claims.claim: Audit's estimate: a few hundred residents in the park extension
claims.found: approximately 491 residents (area-weighted, 2021 DAs)
claims.note: 'a few hundred' for 491 is generous rounding; 'nearly five hundred' would be exact

claims.claim: The minority names the riding 'Rocky Mountain House-Banff Park' and the town of Banff is not in it
claims.found: 'Banff townsite is not in this ED' - ED includes NP land north of the Town of Banff

claims.claim: The Banff townsite and Canmore sit in a minority riding named 'Canmore-Kananaskis'
claims.found: 'the electoral division would include the Town of Banff; ... the Town of Canmore; the Kananaskis Improvement District'

claims.claim: The majority, its own chair among them, called the move 'a bad faith effort' to claim s.15(2) protection, in the commission's official final report
claims.found: 'which is a bad faith effort to ensure it can be protected under s. 15(2) of the Act'
claims.note: quote matches; majority = chair + two (Act s.9 makes the majority's report the commission's report)

claims.claim: 'The communities it was designed to help had to fight for it through public submissions'
claims.note: characterisation; the 56-submission fact behind it is verified above

claims.claim: Banff sits inside a national park on federal land it is not permitted to grow into
claims.found: no repo source on Banff's growth limits (Parks Canada / Banff Incorporation Agreement)
claims.note: true to general knowledge but not sourced in the repo; not web-checked

claims.claim: For provincial purposes almost the only people the province represents in that stretch of the Rockies live in the Banff townsite
claims.found: Banff = 8,305 (2021); Lake Louise hamlet and the ~491 estimated park-extension residents are not netted out
claims.note: 'almost the only' is a loose claim; no repo source states it

claims.claim: Canmore is the next town down the Bow Valley from Banff; Alberta names many divisions for land rather than towns
claims.note: geographic/naming description, not tested

claims.claim: Majority's objection: the extension is 'a bad faith effort' to claim 'a population protection' for land it described as a place 'where no one lives'
claims.found: 'a bad faith effort to ensure it can be protected under s. 15(2)'; 'where no one lives'
claims.note: the two quoted phrases match; 'a population protection' is the report's gloss, not a quoted phrase

claims.claim: Canada counts its population every five years; the 2026 census was taken in spring 2026
claims.found: '2026 Census was collected in May 2026'

claims.claim: Statistics Canada will not release usable data below the provincial level until roughly 2027 or 2028
claims.found: counts 'expected in early 2027'; DA data 'mid-to-late 2027'; detailed tables 'late 2027'
claims.note: repo sources support 2027; '2028' is not in any repo source (hedged 'roughly')

claims.claim: The commission started from the 2021 census, updated to mid-2024 with provincial estimates
claims.found: 2021 census numbers 'updated by the estimated population figures from Alberta Treasury Board'; July 2024 estimate

claims.claim: The census was already four years old when the maps were drawn, potentially fourteen years old when the boundaries retire
claims.found: 'up to 14 years stale at the boundaries' retirement (potentially 2035)'
claims.note: internal tension: academic L2370 says 'ten years old' by 2031 on the same map; the 14-year figure assumes retirement in 2035

claims.claim: Fast-growing cities like Airdrie and Chestermere will change by 40% or more over that window
claims.found: 'moves per-ED population quotas ... by 40 %+ at the 14-year mark under current growth rates'
claims.note: a projection by the audit, not an observed figure

claims.claim: 'Rural communities will shrink'; proposed Act amendment
claims.note: prediction and policy suggestion

claims.claim: 'Neither of these is a finding about the current commission's maps'
Each appendix owns one concept, starts from confusion, ends with what the concept cannot tell you
Appendix A toy example: town of 40,000, four slices of 10,000 against 30,000 rural voters
claims.note: toy numbers, arithmetic only

claims.claim: Finding 1: 85,805 people, four ridings, a minority in three of them
claims.found: Airdrie 85,805 (2024 municipal census); four districts by territory; Airdrie East holds 54.7% so residents are outnumbered in the other three
claims.note: true by territory; Olds-Three Hills-Didsbury holds only ~350 Airdrie residents (0.5%), so by the audit's 2% piece rule it is three pieces

claims.claim: The commission's other (majority) draft shows two ridings were enough
claims.found: majority splits Airdrie in 2 pieces

claims.claim: Cracking describes an effect, not a motive
Section 15(2) lets up to four districts fall below the normal population floor
claims.found: 'no more than 4 of the proposed electoral divisions'

claims.claim: s.15(2) was written for remote districts with strong community ties, like northern ridings serving Indigenous communities
claims.found: Act text states criteria only, no statement of purpose
claims.note: legislative intent is not stated in the Act; no Hansard source with this wording located in the repo

claims.claim: The majority called the minority's extension through national park 'a bad faith effort' to qualify the district for s.15(2)
claims.found: 'a bad faith effort to ensure it can be protected under s. 15(2)'

claims.claim: 'The audit's check undercut the charge:'
claims.note: EDITORIAL DEFECT: the sentence ends with a colon and the next paragraph begins 'Now re-read Finding 2' with nothing in between; text appears to be missing (the audit's population check, ~491 residents, is the likely content)

claims.claim: Finding 2: three shapes, flagged by the commission's majority, confirmed when the audit inspected them
claims.found: majority flagged four boundaries, audit confirmed 3 of 4
claims.note: internal consistency check

claims.claim: Appendix C toy example: 12,000 voters (7,000 O / 5,000 B); evenly drawn Orange wins all three; packed layout gives Orange 1 seat, Blue 2
claims.found: even: 2,333 O vs 1,667 B per district; packed: 4,000-0, then 1,500 O vs 2,500 B twice
claims.note: toy numbers, arithmetic only; checks out

claims.claim: Finding 3: 17 north/east/central Calgary districts, minority 11.5% over provincial average, majority 2.8%
claims.found: Zone A mean 61,225 vs provincial 54,929 = +11.5%; majority Zone A +2.8%
claims.note: 17 districts also stated at reports/public/report_public.md L113

claims.claim: The 'depth half', big winning margins, is missing so no packing signature
claims.found: packing P2 fails on official boundaries: NDP wins 8 of 17 by 15.0 pts vs provincial 27.6

claims.claim: MAD of 3,180 (majority) and 4,707 (minority)
claims.found: Mean absolute deviation from 54,929: 3,180 / 4,707

claims.claim: 4,707 means 'the misses average half again larger'
claims.note: 'half again' = 1.5x; actual 1.48x, fine

claims.claim: Alberta allows +/-25%
claims.found: 'not more than 25% above nor more than 25% below'

claims.claim: The minority map spends 48% more of that currency than the majority
claims.found: 48% more mean absolute deviation (4,707 vs 3,180)

claims.claim: Finding 1 shows the minority 'didn't buy Airdrie's wholeness' with its extra deviation
claims.note: interpretive inference from Finding 1

claims.claim: The '99 of every 100 neutral maps' figure holds only against neutral maps held to +/-12.5%
claims.found: MedAD p99.1 under the +/-12.5% proposal band; p0.013 under the +/-25% band

claims.claim: Every district on both maps is legal (inside the +/-25% band, bar the s.15(2) exceptions)
claims.found: no district crosses the band outside s.15(2) invocations

claims.claim: Ensemble: 252,500 steps in each of four chains, 1,010,000 maps in all
claims.found: '1,010,000 neutral ReCom plans ... 4 chains x 252,500 steps'
claims.note: 4 x 252,500 = 1,010,000; the 'merge two districts and re-split' description is ReCom

claims.claim: No vote data is consulted while drawing the ensemble
claims.found: ReCom proposals use population and contiguity on the 4,765-VA graph; votes used only for scoring
claims.note: not checked line by line in the sampler code

claims.claim: The million maps are worth about 1,400 independent draws
claims.note: 'about 1,400' is at the low end of the stated 1,413-1,522 range

claims.claim: If 69 do, neutral drawing produces such a map 69 times in a million tries
claims.found: 69 of 1,010,000 plans exceed it
claims.note: 69/1,010,000 = 68 per million; fine

claims.claim: Finding 6: majority at the 78th percentile
Finding 6: minority at the 99.99th percentile, 69 of 1,010,000 score higher
claims.found: '69 of 1,010,000 plans exceed it, all at 45/87; p99.99'

claims.claim: The machine does not weigh every fine point of the statute; computer maps are nonpartisan alternatives
Efficiency-gap toy: Orange wins a 100-vote district 90-10, Orange wastes 39 (90-51), Blue wastes 10
claims.found: 90 - 51 = 39; loser wastes all 10
claims.note: toy numbers, arithmetic only

claims.claim: Positive efficiency gaps favour conservatives in this report's sign convention
claims.found: academic report writes the CWEF as 'negative = UCP advantage' in places; the public report defines its own sign and uses it consistently
claims.note: convention differs between the two reports; the public report states its own

claims.claim: The audit's Alberta calibration line (~4.1%) is the level only 5% of the million neutral maps cross
claims.found: 95th-percentile EG = +0.0410 as registered (2026-07-12 rerun gives +0.0408)
claims.note: ~4.1% either way

claims.claim: Finding 7: minority at +4.0%, the 94.5th percentile, below the pre-registered line
claims.found: minority EG +3.96%, p94.54; threshold 4.10%
claims.note: 3.96 rounds to 4.0; 94.54 rounds to 94.5

claims.claim: The audit uses four metrics and a locked threshold
claims.found: four partisan-fairness metrics (EG, mean-median, declination, seats@50/50)

claims.claim: The Ch1 number is 'one in 568,000' (at most)
claims.found: Ch1 p = 8.80e-07; Bonferroni upper bound p <= 1.76e-06

claims.claim: DNA example: one-in-a-million profile, city of ten million, about ten matches, 90% chance someone else is the source
claims.found: 10,000,000 x 1e-6 = 10 matches; 9 of 10 others = 90%
claims.note: toy numbers; assumes no other evidence, as the text says ('on the DNA alone')

claims.claim: Swapping P(evidence|innocence) for P(innocence|evidence) is the prosecutor's fallacy
claims.note: well-established term

claims.claim: Finding 8: audit states the rarity under neutral drawing and refuses to turn it into a verdict
ReCom has a documented lean toward compact, tidy districts
claims.found: 'spanning-tree ReCom's documented compactness weighting (DeFord, Duchin & Solomon 2021, section 4)'

claims.claim: The replacement sampler grows districts from random spanning forests; registered publicly as OSF he53s before any map was drawn with it
claims.found: he53s = 'Forest-ReCom Sampler Robustness Check', registered_utc 2026-07-10T05:42Z (= 2026-07-09 23:42 MDT), public, executed 2026-07-10

claims.claim: Seeds were derived from a public randomness beacon
claims.found: seeds derived from drand round 5,500,000

claims.claim: It moved less than one percentile point on every metric: a pre-registered ROBUST verdict
claims.found: EG 0.81 pp, mean-median 0.34, declination 0.04, seats 0.11 (all < 2 pp = Robust)
claims.note: max shift 0.81 pp, so 'less than one point' holds. But reports/academic/report_academic.md L1077 calls the result 'inconclusive at this run size, not a finding of robustness'; the public text hedges ('shifts that small sit inside its margin of error') yet still leads with ROBUST

claims.claim: That run drew fewer effective samples than registered
claims.found: pooled n_eff 61-124 against a >=200 target

claims.claim: The claim that Act I's flagged geometry is the specific mechanism behind the seat numbers did not survive testing and was dropped
claims.found: mechanism claim dropped (drain test and related checks)
claims.note: internal-consistency check only; the underlying test chain was not rerun here

claims.claim: Finding 9: three attacks, two survived, one claim lost
claims.found: three attacks reported in Finding 9
claims.note: internal consistency

claims.claim: Appendix J: swing-zone test p = 0.0024 under the naive null
claims.found: bootstrap p = 0.0024 (standard i.i.d.-flip permutation)

claims.claim: Under the corrected (block-permutation) null p is about 0.19
claims.found: 'block-permutation p ~ 0.19'

claims.claim: 100 clustered areas are 'more like 20 informative observations wearing 100 coats'
claims.note: illustrative figure, not a measured effective n; academic L1157: the 2,110 swing-zone VAs form one connected component of 2,086

claims.claim: The test was retired
claims.found: 'SZAT is therefore retired as a confirmatory channel'

claims.claim: Finding 10: two instruments retired and one pre-registered test the minority passed outright
claims.found: SZAT and Fisher combination retired; neighbour-drain PASS
claims.note: internal consistency

claims.claim: Correction says nothing against the ensemble findings, which never assumed independence
Minority report says Cochrane residents 'move fluidly' into Calgary
claims.found: 'where residents move fluidly between jurisdictions for work, education, health care, and commerce'
claims.note: quote matches; source says residents move fluidly 'between jurisdictions' along the Calgary-Cochrane corridor

claims.claim: About a third of Cochrane's workers commute into Calgary; roughly half work in Cochrane
Minority says rural residents near Red Deer 'go to school' in the city
claims.found: 'the urban community where they work, go to school, and gather at community events'
claims.note: quote matches

claims.claim: School-division maps put Sylvan Lake and Red Deer in different public divisions, though one Catholic division serves both
claims.found: Chinook's Edge vs Red Deer Public; Red Deer Catholic Regional serves both

claims.claim: 'In most of the six cases we checked' the particular line is where the reason falls short
claims.found: recount: 2 of 6 fail on population arithmetic (Airdrie, Olds), 2 partly supported (Cochrane, Red Deer-Sylvan Lake), 1 not tested (RMH-Banff Park), 1 has no stated rationale (St. Albert-Sturgeon); 'the rationale check separates the redraws; it does not condemn them all'
claims.note: 'most of six' is stronger than the academic recount (2 clear failures, 2 partial); the earlier 'five of six failed' reading was withdrawn. Suggest 'in several of the six' or give the 2/2/1/1 split

claims.claim: Finding 11: the same recipe applied to six stated reasons
claims.found: six contested minority redraws

claims.claim: Chair plus commissioners nominated from the government and opposition sides
claims.found: chair appointed by LGIC; four others appointed by Speaker, nominated by President of Executive Council (2) and Leader of the Opposition (2)

claims.claim: From 1995 to 2017 each commission sent the Assembly one map, even when a commissioner dissented
claims.found: 2017 confirmed: Commissioner Day filed a minority report in Appendix A of a single report. 1992 and 2003 PDFs contain no dissent; 1995 and 2010 reports not in the repo
claims.note: partly supported (2017 and the 1995 s.9 provision); each cycle not individually confirmed

claims.claim: This cycle the room split along its nomination lines; the government's nominees produced the outlier
claims.found: minority = Martin and Evans (both nominated by the President of Executive Council); majority = chair + Clark + Samson

claims.claim: Assembly appointment notice names Julian Martin and John D. Evans, KC as 'Nominated by the President of Executive Council' (March 28, 2025)
claims.found: 'Dr. Julian Martin (Sherwood Park) Nominated by the President of Executive Council John D. Evans, KC (City of Lethbridge) Nominated by the President of Executive Council'
claims.note: quote and URL (canonical link in the saved HTML) match

claims.claim: No evidence in the record shows the government directed or knew of its nominees' map
claims.note: absence-of-evidence statement, scoped to 'this audit's record'

claims.claim: Under the Act the commission proposes and the Assembly disposes; the report has no legal effect until the Assembly enacts a map
claims.found: s.11: if the Assembly by resolution approves or approves with alterations, the Government shall introduce a Bill

claims.claim: The Act places no limits on what the Assembly does instead: no minimum debate, notice period, obligation to prefer the commission, or hearing requirement
claims.found: Act contains no such provisions; s.11 only governs the approval path
claims.note: absence claim; checked by reading all 12 pages

claims.claim: Government Motion 37 referred the work onward to a select committee
claims.found: 'a Select Special Committee on Electoral Boundaries be established to oversee an independent review ... without a requirement to direct the holding of public hearings'; question put on GM 37 on April 21, 2026

claims.claim: MLAs, not an independent commission, oversaw the advisory panel that drew the new map
claims.found: committee: Mr. Lunty (chair), 3 government, 2 opposition MLAs; 'engage independent advisors ... independent advisory panel'

claims.claim: In every cycle since 1995 it was the Assembly's restraint, not the statute, that kept politicians' hands off the pen
claims.found: Act confirms the legal freedom; no repo source reviews each post-1995 Assembly response (1996, 2003, 2010, 2017)
claims.note: the legal half is verified, the historical half ('every cycle') is not sourced in the repo

claims.claim: Finding 13: sixteen communities of hearings replaced by a body required to hold none
claims.found: '28 hearings were held in 16 different locations' (pre-interim round)
claims.note: 16 locations is the first round only; the second round added virtual hearings plus Calgary and Edmonton

claims.claim: The 'November tests' are built to inform the political question
The Supreme Court described the law/convention divide in the 1981 Patriation Reference: courts may recognize a convention yet decline to enforce it
claims.source: evidence/law/ (case not present); web knowledge: Reference re Resolution to Amend the Constitution, [1981] 1 SCR 753
claims.found: not in the repo's evidence/law folder
claims.note: well-known holding and standard citation, but the case was neither in the repo nor fetched; verified_by: web (unchecked)

claims.claim: Decades of practice, federally and in the provinces, built the rule that politicians do not draw their own ridings; some jurisdictions give a commission's map effect unless the legislature overrides it
claims.found: repo holds other jurisdictions' acts but this specific comparison was not located
claims.note: not traced to a specific statute in the repo; the Alberta s.11 contrast is verified

claims.claim: Alberta's Act does not give the commission's map effect
claims.found: Assembly must approve by resolution and Government introduce a Bill

claims.claim: 'A norm violated once, without consequence, is weaker for every government that follows'
Finding 14: real violation, documented, no convention a court will enforce; a court can still review the map
claims.note: legal characterisation; consistent with the Carter (1991) / Charter s.3 framing elsewhere in the report; not independently retested

claims.claim: 'Unenforceable' is a statement about courts, not about consequences
Methodology relies on established political science and legal literature
Chen, Jowei, and Jonathan Rodden. 2013. 'Unintentional Gerrymandering: Political Geography and Electoral Bias in Legislatures.' Quarterly Journal of Political Science 8(3): 239-269
claims.found: identical citation text

claims.claim: Courtney, John C. 2001. Commissioned Ridings: Designing Canada's Electoral Districts. Montreal and Kingston: McGill-Queen's University Press
claims.found: identical citation text

claims.claim: References list holds only two works though the intro promises 'key references' and the heading is 'References & Methodology'
claims.note: EDITORIAL: academic report cites many more (Stephanopoulos-McGhee, DeFord-Duchin-Solomon, Warrington, etc.); no Methodology subsection follows the heading; Appendix E is absent (letters skip D to F) with no cross-reference to it anywhere
